DNA polymerase, on the other hand, plays a crucial role in the process of replication, which is the duplication of the entire DNA molecule before cell division. DNA polymerase also has proofreading activity, which allows it to correct any errors made during replication by removing mismatched nucleotides and replacing them with the correct ones.

In summary, the primary difference between RNA polymerase and DNA polymerase lies in their respective roles in the central dogma of molecular biology.
